# DBUI Design System
# Distribution URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/muditmittal/dbui/main/packages/dbui/llms.txt
#
# DBUI is Databricks' component library — 46 components, 451 icons, 162 tokens.
# Built on shadcn/ui + Base UI + Tailwind CSS v4, reskinned with DuBois design tokens.

## INSTALL

DBUI ships pre-bundled. Installing it is **clone + copy + tsconfig alias**. Nothing else. **No `npm install` is required for DBUI itself or any of its dependencies** — Base UI, CVA, clsx, tailwind-merge, sonner, vaul are all inlined into `packages/dbui/dist/`.

This is intentional: many consumer environments (Databricks corp network in particular) firewall `registry.npmjs.org`. The install path below works without any registry access.

The install has two parts:

1. **Bootstrap** — a one-time prerequisite to set up React + Tailwind v4. **Skip if you already have a working React project.**
2. **Add DBUI** — the actual install. Always required.

If DBUI is being added to an existing project, jump directly to ["Add DBUI"](#add-dbui).

---

## Bootstrap (only if starting from scratch)

DBUI is UI code only. Do NOT scaffold a framework on behalf of the user.

- **If `package.json` already exists with React and Tailwind v4** → skip this section, go to ["Add DBUI"](#add-dbui).
- **If there is no `package.json`** → STOP. Ask the user. If they confirm, suggest:
  ```bash
  npm create vite@latest . -- --template react-ts
  npm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite
  ```
  This is the only `npm install` in the whole flow. It runs once, creates the project shell, and is never needed again. **If this fails because the registry is firewalled, the user must resolve their network access first** — DBUI cannot scaffold a React project for them.

### DO NOT install any of these. They are not DBUI dependencies.

Heavyweight starters: `next-forge`, `create-t3-app`, `create-next-app --example …`, any Vercel template that auto-adds vendors.
Security / auth: **Arcjet**, Clerk, Auth0, NextAuth, Descope, Supabase Auth.
Databases / ORMs: Prisma, Drizzle, Convex, Supabase, Neon, Turso.
State / data libs: Redux, Zustand, Jotai, React Query, SWR, Apollo.
AI SDKs: Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, OpenAI SDK.
Icon packs: lucide-react, @heroicons/react, react-icons — DBUI already has 451 icons.
UI libs: shadcn CLI, Radix, Mantine, Chakra, MUI — DBUI replaces these.

If the user explicitly asks for one of the above later, fine. Never add any of them proactively.

---

## Add DBUI

Five steps. None of them require `npm install`.

### Step 1: Sync DBUI into the project

```bash
if [ -d ~/dbui/.git ]; then
  (cd ~/dbui && git pull --ff-only)
else
  git clone https://github.com/muditmittal/dbui.git ~/dbui
fi
cp -r ~/dbui/packages/dbui ./dbui
cp -r ~/dbui/packages/dbui-shells ./dbui-shells
```

This block is **idempotent — run it for first install AND every update.** It clones if `~/dbui` doesn't exist yet, pulls latest if it does, then copies the freshly-synced source into the project. The pre-built `./dbui/dist/` ships in git — no build step, no `npm install`.

### Step 2: Add path aliases to `tsconfig.json`

Point `dbui/*` at the **pre-built dist**, and `dbui-shells/*` at its source:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "paths": {
      "dbui/*": ["./dbui/dist/*"],
      "dbui/components/icons/*": ["./dbui/src/components/icons/*"],
      "dbui/tokens/*": ["./dbui/src/tokens/*"],
      "dbui-shells/*": ["./dbui-shells/src/*"]
    }
  }
}
```

Vite/Webpack projects: mirror the same aliases in `resolve.alias`.

Why icons and tokens stay on `src/`:
- **Icons** are 451 individual `.tsx` files; we don't pre-bundle them so consumers tree-shake naturally and can read source on hover.
- **Tokens** are pure CSS (`globals.css`) — no JS to bundle.

### Step 3: Import DBUI tokens in root CSS

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "./dbui/src/tokens/globals.css";
```

### Step 4: Install DBUI skills (Cursor users)

```bash
mkdir -p .cursor/skills
cp -r ./dbui/skills/* .cursor/skills/
```

This copies 4 skill files that teach the AI assistant how to pick components, pick icons, build full screens, and validate code against DBUI rules. Without these, the agent works from CLAUDE.md alone — with them, it has structured workflows for screen building and validation.

For Claude Code users: skills aren't needed — CLAUDE.md and the `docs/` folder provide equivalent guidance.

### Step 5: Wire up AI assistant rules ([see "Make AI assistants prioritize DBUI"](#make-ai-assistants-prioritize-dbui))

Without this, your AI assistant won't know DBUI exists and will keep generating raw `<button>` and `<div>` elements. Critical for adoption.

### Step 6: Create the first page with the Base Shell

```tsx
import { Base } from "dbui-shells"

export default function Home() {
  return (
    <Base defaultActive="catalog">
      <div style={{ display: "flex", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", height: "100%" }}>
        <p style={{ fontSize: 13, color: "#6F6F6F" }}>DBUI is installed. Start building here.</p>
      </div>
    </Base>
  )
}
```

Then start the dev server (`npm run dev`, `yarn dev`, whatever the project already uses). The full Databricks shell renders. Done.

### Updating later

Re-run **Step 1** (sync) and **Step 4** (skills copy). That same pair is the update path — Step 1 pulls latest source, Step 4 refreshes the skills. No separate update procedure.

Steps 2 (tsconfig aliases), 3 (CSS import), 5 (AI rules wiring), and 6 (first page) only need to be done once.

---

## Make AI assistants prioritize DBUI

This is the part most consumers miss. Dropping the `dbui/` folder into a project doesn't automatically tell Claude / Cursor / Copilot to use DBUI components instead of generating raw HTML or pulling shadcn. You have to point them at the rules.

### If you DO NOT have a `CLAUDE.md` at the project root

Just copy DBUI's:

```bash
cp ./dbui/CLAUDE.md ./CLAUDE.md
```

Done. Cursor and Claude Code both auto-load `CLAUDE.md` at session start.

### If you ALREADY have a `CLAUDE.md` at the project root

**Do NOT overwrite it.** Append a DBUI section instead. Either:

**Option A — inline** (concise, gets read in full):
Open your existing `./CLAUDE.md` and append the contents of `./dbui/CLAUDE.md`. Add a heading like `## DBUI — Design System Rules` so the section is named.

**Option B — by reference** (smaller, less guaranteed to be obeyed):
Append this to your existing `./CLAUDE.md`:

```md
## DBUI — Design System Rules

This project uses DBUI for all UI. **Read `./dbui/CLAUDE.md` before writing any UI code.** Key rules:

- Always use components from `dbui/components/ui/*`. Never raw `<button>`, `<input>`, `<div role="dialog">`.
- Always use icons from `dbui/components/icons/{Name}`. Never lucide, heroicons, or any other icon package.
- Always use semantic tokens (`bg-primary`, `text-foreground`). Never hardcode hex colors.
- Every page wraps in `<Base>` from `dbui-shells`.
- Base UI uses `render={<Component />}`, not Radix `asChild`.

Full rules: `./dbui/CLAUDE.md`. Component picker: `./dbui/docs/component-index.md`. Icon picker: `./dbui/docs/icon-index.md`.
```

Option A is more reliable because the LLM gets the full rule set in context. Option B is enough for most cases and keeps your root CLAUDE.md slim.

### For Cursor specifically (more reliable enforcement)

In addition to (or instead of) the root CLAUDE.md, create `.cursor/rules/dbui.mdc`:

```mdc
---
description: DBUI design system rules — use DBUI components, never raw HTML
globs: ["**/*.tsx", "**/*.jsx"]
alwaysApply: true
---

(paste the contents of ./dbui/CLAUDE.md here)
```

`alwaysApply: true` + a TSX/JSX glob means the rule fires on every UI file, every time. This catches cases where the LLM forgets the root CLAUDE.md mid-session.

### For Claude Code

The root `CLAUDE.md` approach (above) is the default mechanism. No additional config needed — Claude Code reads `./CLAUDE.md` at session start and recursively reads `CLAUDE.md` files in any directory it touches. Since DBUI ships its own `./dbui/CLAUDE.md`, that file is also picked up automatically when Claude Code edits files in or near `./dbui/`.

### For GitHub Copilot / Cody / generic LLMs without CLAUDE.md support

These tools rely on docstrings and code comments. The DBUI rules embedded in `@guideline` and `@constraint` JSDoc on each component still get surfaced via autocomplete. For higher-level prioritization, add a section to your project `README.md`:

> ## UI components
>
> This project uses DBUI. Import all UI primitives from `dbui/components/ui/*` and icons from `dbui/components/icons/*`. Never use raw HTML interactive elements. See `./dbui/CLAUDE.md` for rules.

### Will my existing project work after adding DBUI?

Yes, with these prerequisites:

| Requirement | Why |
|---|---|
| **React 18+ and react-dom 18+** | DBUI's `package.json` declares them as peerDependencies |
| **Tailwind v4** (not v3) | DBUI uses v4-only token features (`@import "tailwindcss"`, OKLCH semantic tokens). If you're on v3, migrate first using the [Tailwind v4 upgrade guide](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide), then add DBUI |
| **A bundler that supports path aliases** | Vite, Next.js, Webpack, Parcel, Rspack — all fine. Plain `tsc` without a bundler will not work |
| **No conflicting global CSS resets** | If your project has aggressive resets (e.g. `* { all: revert; }`), DBUI's tokens may be overridden. Reset rules should be scoped, not universal |

DBUI coexists fine with other UI libraries you might already have (Material UI, Chakra, etc.) — it just adds its own components, doesn't try to replace theirs at runtime. New code you write should use DBUI; old code can stay until you migrate it.

---

## WHERE TO LOOK — read these BEFORE writing any UI

These are the discovery layer. Each component's source file (`dbui/src/components/ui/<name>.tsx`) is the rules layer — read its `@guideline` and `@constraint` JSDoc when you actually use the component.

| Need | Canonical file |
|------|---------------|
| Pick the right component | `./dbui/docs/component-index.md` — searchable component table (category, when to use, avoid for, synonyms) |
| Find the right icon | `./dbui/docs/icon-index.md` — searchable 449-icon index |
| Write any user-facing copy | `./dbui/docs/brandvoice.md` — vocabulary, tone, microcopy templates |
| Pick a page-level layout / shell | `./dbui/composition.md` — five named shells with regions, scaling, scroll, primary action |
| Apply cross-cutting layout/spacing rules | `./dbui/docs/component-rules.md` — spacing rhythm, page padding, icon and button rules |
| Read full guidelines/constraints for a component | `./dbui/src/components/ui/<name>.tsx` — `@guideline` / `@constraint` JSDoc |
| Get entity icons for trees | `./dbui/src/components/icons/entity-icons.ts` — NEVER guess these |
| Design token values | `./dbui/src/tokens/globals.css` |

**Single source of truth:** per-component rules live ONLY in the component's JSDoc. Per-icon details live ONLY in `icon-index.md`. Cross-cutting layout rules live ONLY in `component-rules.md`. Shell-level composition lives ONLY in `composition.md`. Voice/tone lives ONLY in `brandvoice.md`. If you ever see a rule duplicated, the more specific source wins (JSDoc > index > llms.txt).

---

## RULES (non-negotiable, cross-cutting)

These are global truths — every component obeys them. Per-component rules are in JSDoc.

1. ALWAYS use DBUI components. NEVER use raw `<button>`, `<input>`, `<div role="dialog">`.
2. ALWAYS use icons from `dbui/components/icons/{Name}`. NEVER install lucide, heroicons, etc.
3. ALWAYS use semantic tokens (`bg-primary`, `text-foreground`). NEVER hardcode hex colors.
4. ALWAYS import from `dbui/components/ui/{component}`. NEVER import @radix-ui or @base-ui directly.
5. Every page starts with `<Base>` from `dbui-shells`. NEVER build header/nav from scratch.
6. For hierarchical data, use `DataTreeView` or `FileTreeView`. NEVER fake trees with nested divs.
7. Base UI uses `render` prop, NOT Radix `asChild`:
   ```tsx
   <DialogTrigger render={<Button />}>Open</DialogTrigger>       // correct
   <DialogTrigger asChild><Button>Open</Button></DialogTrigger>   // WRONG — ignored by Base UI
   ```
8. Read `brandvoice.md` before writing any user-facing string. No emoji in product UI. No exclamation marks. No "utilize" / "leverage" / "seamless".

---

## ONE-LINE REMINDERS

These are facts agents forget most often. Full rules are in the canonical files in WHERE TO LOOK above — don't re-derive from these one-liners, look them up.

- **Base font is 13px, not 14px.** Body: `text-[13px] leading-[20px]`. Captions: `text-[12px] leading-[16px]`. Page title: `text-[22px] font-semibold`. Section heading: `text-[18px] font-semibold`. → full table in `docs/component-rules.md`.
- **Spacing rhythm: 8 / 16 / 24.** Inside a component: `gap-2`. Between form fields and sections: `gap-4`. Between major blocks: `gap-6`. → full table in `docs/component-rules.md`.
- **Surfaces.** Shell background: `bg-muted`. Content surface: `bg-background border rounded-md`. Page padding inside the surface: `px-6 py-4`. → `docs/component-rules.md` → "Platform Shell".
- **Three-column detail.** Tree (260px) · main (flex-1) · metadata sidebar (280px). Each scrolls independently. → `composition.md` → "Shell E".
- **Icons.** Categories are `object` / `action` / `indicator` / `component`. Always search `docs/icon-index.md` before inserting any icon. Never guess. Commonly confused: Experiments → `Beaker`, Jobs → `Workflows`, Compute → `Cloud`, Unity Catalog → `Catalog`, Genie → `SparkleDouble`, SQL Warehouse → `Database`, Marketplace → `Storefront`. → full table in `docs/icon-index.md`.

## KNOWN GAPS

Not yet available — compose from primitives as interim:
- DatePicker, Stepper, Banner, CodeBlock, Virtualized lists
- **Chart** (`recharts` not bundled — non-critical)
- **Resizable** / **ResizablePanel** (`react-resizable-panels` not bundled — non-critical)
